title: One-Pan Creamy Tuscan Gnocchi: Ready in 15 Minutes
description: Skip the sink full of dishes with this 15-minute creamy tuscan gnocchi. Crispy potato pillows swimming in a garlicky parmesan sauce. Totally foolproof.
story: It was past 7:30 PM, my kitchen was already a disaster zone from morning coffee, and I refused to wash three different pots. That is the exact moment this one-pan creamy tuscan gnocchi was born. I didn't even bother boiling the little potato pillows first—shelf-stable gnocchi crisps up surprisingly well if you just let it sit in a hot skillet with a little avocado oil. Toss in some garlic, a handful of baby spinach, and a scoop of whatever grated parmesan is hiding in the dairy drawer. Boom. Dinner is done, my small apartment dishwasher is spared, and I get to eat on the couch in peace.
ingredients: 1 package (16 oz) shelf-stable potato gnocchi (Trader Joe's brand works great)
2 tablespoons unsalted butter (Kerrygold if you're feeling fancy)
1/2 cup sundried tomatoes, drained and sliced
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste
instructions: Step 1: Melt the butter with a splash of avocado oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Toss in the dry gnocchi straight from the package—no boiling required! Let them cook undisturbed for about 5 minutes until golden brown on one side.

Step 2: Turn the heat down to medium-low. Add the minced garlic and sundried tomatoes, stirring constantly for about 60 seconds until that amazing garlic aroma hits you. (The first time I tested this, I cranked the burner too high and burnt the garlic, so keep it gentle here!)
Step 3: Pour in the heavy cream and let it gently simmer for 3 minutes until it starts to thicken up and coat the back of a spoon.
Step 4: Stir in the parmesan cheese until melted and smooth, then fold in the baby spinach until it wilts right into the sauce. Season with salt and pepper, and serve immediately.
proHack: Do not skip the step of letting the dry gnocchi brown directly in the butter and oil. It creates a crispy outer crust while keeping the inside pillowy soft. If you add the cream too early, you lose that texture completely.
storage: Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for up to 2 days. To reheat, toss it back into a skillet over low heat with a splash of milk or water to loosen up the parmesan sauce—microwaving makes the cream separate and gets weird.

faqs.question: Can I use frozen gnocchi instead of shelf-stable?
faqs.answer: You definitely can, but give them a quick 2-minute boil first or thaw them completely. Otherwise, the inside stays cold while the outside burns in the skillet.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the cream sauce from curdling?
faqs.answer: Turn the heat down to low right before pouring in the heavy cream and parmesan. High heat will cause the dairy to break and get grainy.
